name: Ransomware Forces EHR Downtime
description: A ransomware actor encrypts clinical systems; the hospital runs paper downtime procedures and diverts ambulances while the EHR is restored.
asset: Electronic health record and clinical systems
assumptions: Downtime lasts 3–14 days with staged clinical restoration.
Patient-safety impacts are handled as a separate (non-financial) analysis.
Secondary loss covers regulatory response, claims, and reputation-driven volume loss.

name: PHI Breach via Vendor Portal
description: An attacker compromises a third-party portal that exchanges protected health information, producing a reportable breach attributed to the organization.
asset: Protected health information shared with vendors
assumptions: A threat event is a compromise at a vendor holding our PHI.
Vulnerability reflects the share of vendors without hardened access.
Secondary loss includes OCR penalties and class-action exposure.

name: Networked Medical Device Compromise
description: An intruder pivots through unpatched networked devices (infusion pumps, imaging); affected fleets are quarantined and clinical schedules disrupted.
asset: Infusion pumps and imaging devices on the clinical network
assumptions: A confirmed device compromise quarantines the affected fleet until revalidated.
Patient-safety impacts are handled as a separate (non-financial) analysis.
Secondary loss covers rescheduled procedures and vendor remediation.

name: Insider Snooping on Patient Records
description: Workforce members access high-profile patient records without a treatment relationship, triggering privacy investigation, discipline, and notification.
assumptions: An incident is access without a documented care relationship.
Vulnerability reflects the chance monitoring misses or delays detection.
Secondary loss includes civil claims from affected patients.

name: Payroll Diversion via Phished HR Portal
description: Credential phishing against the HR self-service portal lets attackers change direct-deposit details and divert staff salaries.
assumptions: A loss event is a campaign that changes at least one deposit record.
Made-whole payments to staff are primary loss.
Secondary loss covers forced resets and workforce trust measures.
